testsuite.name: workshop.vfx.math.core.QuatTest

testcase.name: Quaternion multiplication is associative (as rotations) and composes rotations
Golden: slerp action matches the oracle, also with q1 negated (shortest path)
slerp: endpoints and constant angular speed, with extrapolation
slerp is continuous across the near-parallel (nlerp) threshold and never NaN
axisAngle normalizes non-unit axes and rejects zero or non-finite input
Golden: axisAngle(axis, angle).rotate(v) equals Rodrigues from the Python oracle (2,042 rows)
angleTo recovers the rotation angle, including tiny angles and near pi
Degenerate quaternions: zero and non-finite normalize to identity (M0: no NaN propagation)
Golden: qa.mul(qb).rotate(v) equals Rodrigues(a, Rodrigues(b, v)) (1,500 rows)
nlerp: unit norm, endpoints, shortest sign
shortestArc maps from-direction onto to-direction for random pairs
shortestArc: identical, antiparallel, near-antiparallel and zero inputs (M0: robustness)
fromEulerApplyXThenYThenZ equals the explicit rotation sequence X, then Y, then Z about fixed axes
1,000,000 compositions: periodic renormalization keeps the norm within 1e-12; raw drift is reported
toFrame / fromFrame round trip, including 180-degree rotations (all matrix-to-quaternion branches)
slerp takes the shortest path: q1 and -q1 give the same result
